RESPONSE TO ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S LIST OF INTERVENORS WHO DID NOT
           FILE TESTIMONY OR A STATEMENT OF POSITIION

        TO THE HONORABLE JUDGES BRITE, QUINN AND CHICO:
        COME NOW, Naruna Investments, LLC, Scott’s Alamo, LP, Susan Cornwell and W.
Reegan Busby (Naruna Intervenors) in the above-docketed matter, and file this Response to Oncor
and LCRA TSC’S List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or a Statement of Position,
and would respectfully show the following:
                                                          I.
                                                BACKGROUND
        State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) Order Nos. 6 and 9 established May 15,
2026 as the deadline for Applicants to file a list of intervenors who did not file testimony or a
statement of position. On May 18, Applicants filed their 30-page list, including a reference to W.
Reegan Busby who is part of the Naruna Intervenors group.1 Pursuant to Order No. 1 and title 16

1
 Oncor and LCRA TSC’s List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or a Statement of Position at 8 (May 15,
2026) (Interchange Item No. 4688).

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                                                                                1
PUC Docket No. 59475
Response to List of Intervenors
  Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.78(a), this Response is filed within five working days
 from the receipt of Applicants’ intervenor list and is therefore timely filed.
                                                      II.
                                                 RESPONSE
         W. Reegan Busby’s individual request to intervene was granted on May 6, 2026 and she
 should not be dismissed as a party or prohibited from participating in the hearing on the merits or
 briefing thereafter. Ms. Busby is the daughter of Susan Cornwell who timely filed direct testimony
 (PFT) on behalf of Naruna Investments, LLC, Scott’s Alamo, LP, herself, individually, and her
 daughter Ms. Busby, individually on May 13, 2026. For convenience only, Ms. Cornwell’s PFT
 referenced the group “Naruna Intervenors” to reflect the participation of the whole group, the two
 corporate entities and the two individuals. Ms. Cornwell explains this specifically in her PFT,
 Exhibit SC-1 at 5:6-10 and 16-18. Therefore, Ms. Busby, individually and as a member of the
 Naruna Intervenors did file testimony and her inclusion in Applicants’ list of those intervenors
 who did not file such testimony is in error.
         As further explained in the PFT, Ms. Busby and her husband currently use and enjoy the
 property that has been in Ms. Busby’s family for over 107 years and which is the site of their future
 permanent home and guest house. Ms. Busby had and continues to have a justiciable interest in
 the outcome of this docket and should participate with the other members of the Naruna
 Intervenors’ group with whom she is included and aligned.
                                                      III.
                                                CONCLUSION
         For the reasons set out above, Naruna Intervenors request that the ALJs do not dismiss W.
Reegan Busby as an individual party and member of their group in this proceeding and grant all
other relief to which they are entitled.
                                                Respectfully submitted,

                                                Helen S. Gilbert
